why: This is a periodic review of position descriptions against a fixed duty list, which the council's enterprise Claude can do now from a controlled SharePoint library, with no new system to build or support.
knowledge: The council's position description library (current approved versions) for City Fleet and other branches whose roles touch heavy vehicles.
The council's Chain of Responsibility procedure and CoR duty register, once agreed.
The Heavy Vehicle National Law (Queensland) and the regulator's Chain of Responsibility guidance.
The council's position description template and wording guide from People and Culture.
The council's organisational chart, so each role can be matched to its party type (scheduler, loader, operator, executive and so on).
Transport, haulage and plant hire contract templates, to check CoR clauses for roles that manage contracts.

technical: Move the prototype into an Azure DevOps repo and rebuild the front end in Vue and Bootstrap, hosted on Azure App Service with council (Entra ID) sign-in.

Move all AI calls into an Azure Function App, with Claude through Microsoft Foundry or the council's Anthropic agreement (an ICT-DA exception, as it's outside the listed stack). Keys live in Key Vault, never in the page.
Swap names, email addresses and phone numbers for placeholders before a position description goes to the model.
Pull approved position descriptions from the council's HR system or its document library through Boomi or Logic Apps (read only), and store the text in Blob Storage.
Keep the CoR duty register, role to party type mapping, review results and officer overrides in Azure SQL, with an audit trail of who changed what.
Index the Heavy Vehicle National Law extracts, regulator guidance and the council's CoR procedure in Azure AI Search, so each finding can cite its source.
Check every AI quote against the position description text (as the prototype does) and log the pass rate in Application Insights.
Power BI report over the SQL results for the coverage matrix by branch, for the CoR steering group.
Security review against the OWASP Top 10 and the OWASP Top 10 for LLM apps, including prompt injection from uploaded documents.
Dev, Test and Prod resource groups, cost alerts, and Azure DevOps CI/CD pipelines for each environment.
business: Confirm the business owner (City Fleet manager or the CoR steering group), the scope (which branches and roles) and success measures, such as percent of high-risk duties covered and time to review a branch.
Agree the CoR duty register and party type for each role with the CoR lead and Legal Services.
Name People and Culture as the process owner for any position description changes, and agree the wording guide.
Build a test plan and an AI evaluation set (30 or so real-style position descriptions, anonymised, with expert-marked coverage), then run UAT with the CoR lead and HR business partners.
Train the CoR lead and HR business partners, and set up support: who to ask and how to report a wrong result.
Get ICT-DA, CAB, PGG and Business System Owner approval, with a Go Live plan, service transition document and support playbook.

technical: Set up a Claude Project for the CoR review in the council's enterprise Claude, with the prototype's rules (quote the exact line, never invent evidence, suggest wording only for gaps) as the project instructions.
Add the CoR duty register, the council's CoR procedure, the regulator's guidance and the position description template as project files.
Connect the SharePoint library that holds approved position descriptions with the Microsoft 365 connector, read only.
Build a Claude skill that checks one position description or a whole branch and returns the coverage matrix, gap summary and suggested wording in the council's format.
Admin settings checked: data retention, sharing, connector permissions, and that only role documents (not staff files) are in scope.
business: Confirm the business owner, who will use it (CoR lead, HR business partners, branch managers) and what it must never do (it suggests, People and Culture decides).
Agree the duty register and each role's party type with the CoR lead and Legal Services before the first review.
Test it on 20 to 30 position descriptions already reviewed by hand and record how often it agrees.
Pilot with City Fleet for one review cycle, then extend to Road Maintenance, Depot Operations, Procurement and Waste Services.
Enterprise Claude seats for the CoR lead and HR business partners.
A project owner who keeps the duty register, instructions and templates current when the law or guidance changes.
Get the use case approved (ICT-DA and PGG) and confirm privacy settings before rolling it out wider.
